[[Campeonato Carioca|Carioca]], 1st of 12 | website = {{URL|https://www.flamengo.com.br/|flamengo.com.br}} | current = {{CURRENTYEAR}} CR Flamengo season | pattern_la1 = _flamengo26h | pattern_b1 = _flamengo26h | pattern_ra1 = _flamengo26h | pattern_sh1 = _flamengo26h | pattern_so1 = _flamengo26hl | leftarm1 = 000000 | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = 000000 | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = FF0000 | pattern_la2 = _flamengo26a | pattern_b2 = _flamengo26a | pattern_ra2 = _flamengo26a | pattern_sh2 = _flamengo26a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _flamengo26t | pattern_b3 = _flamengo26t | pattern_ra3 = _flamengo26t | pattern_sh3 = _adidasred | pattern_so3 = _adidasblackl | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = 000000 | socks3 = FF0000 | American = true }} {{Flamengo sections}} '''Clube de Regatas do Flamengo''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|ˈklubi dʒi ʁeˈɡataz du flaˈmẽɡu|lang}}; {{lit|Flamengo Rowing Club}}), more commonly referred to as simply '''Flamengo''', is a Brazilian multi-sports club based in [[Rio de Janeiro]], in the neighborhood of [[Gávea]]. It was founded in and named after the [[Flamengo, Rio de Janeiro|Flamengo]] neighborhood in 1895, and is best known for its professional [[association football|football]] team. Flamengo is one of two clubs to have [[List of unrelegated association football clubs|never been relegated]] from Brazil's [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|top division]], along with [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]], and the most popular football club in Brazil with more than 46.9 million fans, equivalent to 21.9% of the population that supports a team in Brazil.{{Cite web |date=7 March 2024 |title=Qual é a maior torcida do Brasil em 2024 |url=https://placar.com.br/placar/qual-e-a-maior-torcida-do-pais-em-2024-veja-o-que-diz-nova-pesquisa/#:~:text=Na%20primeira%20posi%C3%A7%C3%A3o%2C%20aparece%20o,que%20torce%20para%20algum%20time. |access-date=12 April 2024 |website=Agenda Bafafá}} The club was first established in 1895 specifically as a [[Rowing (sport)|rowing]] club in the Flamengo neighborhood and did not play its first official football match until 1912. Flamengo's traditional uniform features red and black striped shirts with white shorts, and red and black striped socks. Flamengo has typically played its home matches in the [[Maracanã Stadium]] (which also often hosts the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]]) since its completion in 1950. Since 1969, the [[New World vulture|vulture]] (Portuguese: ''urubu'') has been the [[mascot]] of Flamengo. Flamengo is Brazil's richest and most valuable football club with an annual revenue of [[Brazilian real|R$]]1.2 billion (€218 million){{Cite web |title=Flamengo arrecada R$ 1,2 bi como europeu, mas só atinge elite com Liga |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/colunas/rodrigo-mattos/2023/04/01/flamengo-arrecada-r-12-bi-como-europeu-mas-so-atinge-elite-com-liga.htm |access-date=2 March 2023 |website=www.uol.com.br |language=pt-br}} and a valuation of over R$5,096 billion (€800 million).{{Cite web |title=Flamengo lidera lista de clubes mais valiosos do Brasil |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/esportes/futebol/flamengo-lidera-lista-de-clubes-mais-valiosos-do-brasil-veja-ranking/ |access-date=15 December 2025 |website=cnnbrasil.com.br|date=9 December 2025 }} Flamengo is the non-European football club with the most followers on social media, with 65 million followers across all platforms as of 2 December 2025,{{cite web | url=https://www.iboperepucom.com/br/rankings/ranking-digital-dos-clubes-brasileiros-dez-2025/ | title=Digital Ranking of Brazilian Clubs | date=2 December 2025 }} and also the most successful Brazilian team of the 21st century so far.{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Alexandre |date=12 April 2023 |title=Vasco tem perdido espaço como maior rival de flamenguistas, mostra pesquisa |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/esportes/vasco-tem-perdido-espaco-como-maior-rival-de-flamenguistas-mostra-pesquisa/ |access-date=2 January 2024 |website=CNN Brasil}}{{Cite web |date=20 April 2022 |title=Colunistas opinam: Palmeiras já superou Vasco como maior rival do Flamengo? |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2022/04/20/colunistas-opinam-palmeiras-ja-superou-vasco-como-maior-rival-do-flamengo.htm |access-date=2 January 2024 |website=uol.com.br |language=pt-br}}{{Cite web |date=8 November 2023 |title=Flamengo x Palmeiras é a maior rivalidade interestadual? Colunistas debatem |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2023/11/08/flamengo-x-palmeiras-e-a-maior-rivalidade-interestadual-colunistas-debatem.htm |access-date=2 January 2024 |website=UOL |language=pt-br}} The club is also one of the most successful in Brazilian football, having amassed a considerable array of national and international titles. The clubs's training center, officially known as "[[Ninho do Urubu]]" ("Vulture's Nest"), is located in [[Vargem Grande, Rio de Janeiro|Vargem Grande]], Rio de Janeiro. It serves as the primary training facility for the Flamengo football club, housing its professional teams and [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo (youth)|youth academy]].{{Cite web |date=8 February 2019 |title=Fire at Flamengo's centre kills 10 youth players |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37569539/flamengo-training-centre-fire-rio-de-janeiro-kills-10-youth-players |access-date=27 August 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Flamengo's youth academy is one of the most prolific in Brazil and in the world, having developed a number of Brazilian internationals such as [[Zico (footballer)|Zico]], [[Zizinho]], [[Vinícius Júnior]], [[Lucas Paquetá]], [[Júlio César (football goalkeeper, born 1979)|Júlio César]], [[Adriano (footballer, born February 1982)|Adriano]], [[Mário Zagallo]], [[Léo Júnior|Júnior]] and [[Leonardo Araújo|Leonardo]]. Flamengo has also been well represented in the Brazil national team; at the [[1938 FIFA World Cup]], forward [[Leônidas (footballer, born 1913)|Leônidas da Silva]], a Flamengo player at the time, was the [[FIFA World Cup Golden Boot|Golden Boot]] winner with 7 goals and won the [[FIFA World Cup Golden Ball|Golden Ball]], thus becoming the first Brazilian player ever to win those two awards. Twelve years later at the [[1950 FIFA World Cup|1950 World Cup]], Zizinho, a [[midfielder]] for Flamengo, also won the Golden Ball after he was voted best player. Four out of the ten top scorers for Brazil have been Flamengo players at one point in their careers, seven players have won the World Cup whilst playing for Flamengo, and Flamengo player Mário Zagallo scored Brazil's third goal in the [[1958 FIFA World Cup final|1958 World Cup final]]. ==History== {{Main|History of CR Flamengo}} ===Establishment of the club (1895–1912)=== Flamengo was founded on 17 November 1895, by a group of rowers gathered at club member Nestor de Barros's manor on [[Flamengo, Rio de Janeiro|Flamengo Beach]] in Rio de Janeiro. In the late 19th century, [[Rowing (sport)|rowing]] was the most played sport in the city. Previously, they could only afford a used boat named ''Pherusa'', which had to be completely rebuilt before it could be used in competition. The team debuted on 6 October 1895, when they sailed off the [[Caju, Rio de Janeiro|Caju Point]] toward Flamengo Beach. However, strong winds turned over the boat and the rowers nearly drowned. They were rescued by a fishing boat named ''Leal'' (Loyal). Later as the ''Pherusa'' was undergoing repairs, it was stolen and never found again. The group saved money to buy a new boat, the ''Etoile'', renamed ''Scyra''. On the night of 17 November, the group gathered at Nestor de Barros's manor on Flamengo beach and founded the ''Grupo de Regatas do Flamengo'' (English: ''Flamengo Rowing Group'') and elected its first board and president (Domingos Marques de Azevedo). The name was changed a few weeks later to its current title of ''Clube de Regatas do Flamengo'' (''Flamengo Rowing Club''). The founders decided that the anniversary of the club's foundation should be commemorated on 15 November to coincide with [[Proclamation of the Republic (Brazil)|Republic Proclamation Day]], a national holiday. Flamengo's football team was only established after a group of ten dissatisfied players from [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] broke away from that club following a board dispute.{{Cite web |url=http://seuhistory.com/hoje-na-historia/fundado-o-clube-de-regatas-do-flamengo |title=Fundado o Clube de Regatas do Flamengo |date=17 November 1895 |publisher=History Channel |access-date=1 September 2016}} The players decided to join Flamengo because Alberto Borgerth, the team's captain, was also a rower for Flamengo. Also, establishing a land sports department at Flamengo was preferable to joining football rivals [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] or the all-English club [[Paissandu Atlético Clube|Paissandu]]. The new members were admitted on 8 November 1911. A motion against the club taking part in football tournaments was put to a vote but was defeated, and as a result the members officially established the club's new football department on 24 December 1911. ===Football in the amateur era (1912–1933)=== [[File:Flamengo 1912.jpg|thumb|left|The recently formed [[association football|football]] team before a match vs. Paissandu, 1912]] The new team trained on {{ill|Russel Beach|pt|Praia do Russel}} and gradually gained the support of the locals, who closely watched their practice matches. The first official match was played on 3 May 1912, and marked, to this day, the largest margin of victory in the club's history, as they defeated [[Sport Club Mangueira|Mangueira]] 16–2. Flamengo's first ever match against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]], the start of the [[Fla-Flu]] rivalry, was played on 7 July of that year and was won by Fluminense by a score of 3–2. That same year, Flamengo finished as runners-up of the [[Campeonato Carioca]], the Rio de Janeiro State Championship. The team's first uniform was nicknamed the "''papagaio vintém''", due to its similarity to a particular type of kite. [[File:1914 - Flamengo.jpg|thumb|The Flamengo team of 1914, when the club won its first [[Campeonato Carioca|Carioca championship]]]] In 1914 the club won the Campeonato Carioca for the first time, dressed in a red, black, and white-striped shirt nicknamed the "''cobra coral''" ([[coral snake]]) was worn until 1916. Flamengo won the Campeonato Carioca again the following year, in 1915, and secured their first back-to-back championship; something they also did with their titles in 1920 and 1921. In 1925, the team won the Campeonato Carioca and five other tournaments, a record at the time. In 1927 the prominent Rio newspaper [[Jornal do Brasil]], in partnership with a mineral water company, held a mail-in contest to find "the most beloved club in Brazil." Though Flamengo enjoyed their largest increase in fan support after the club professionalized in the 1930s, they still defeated popular rivals [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]] in the vote.{{Cite web |date=8 September 2017 |title=Flamengo: o mais querido há 90 anos {{!}} Blog Memória EC |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/blogs/especial-blog/memoria-ec/post/flamengo-o-mais-querido-ha-90-anos.html |access-date=13 March 2019 |website=globoesporte.com |language=pt-br}} This was the first of many times that Flamengo would be voted as the nation's most popular club, inspiring the nickname "''o mais querido do Brasil''" ("the most beloved of Brazil").{{Cite web |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2015/11/fla-120-anos-o-clube-mais-querido-do-brasil-e-2-guerra-mundial.html |title=Fla 120 anos: o "Mais Querido do Brasil" e a Segunda Guerra Mundial |last=Frigols |first=Matheus |website=globoesporte.com |date=15 November 2015 |language=pt-br |access-date=14 March 2019}} In 1933 the team went on its first tour outside Brazil (to [[Montevideo]] and [[Buenos Aires]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesf/flamengo-satrip33.html |title=Rio de la Plata trip of CR Flamengo (Rio de Janeiro) 1933 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |access-date=13 March 2019}}) and on 14 May of the same year played its final match as an amateur team, defeating [[River Futebol Clube]] by a score of 16–2.{{Cite web |url=https://futebolnacional.com.br/infobol/matchdetails.jsp?code=CE458392AC0176169E89E60A7C00AB4D&lang=pt_br |title=Flamengo 16x2 River {{!}} futebolnacional.com.br |last=Rodrigues |first=Gerson |website=futebolnacional.com.br |access-date=13 March 2019}} After this, the club's football department became professional. ===Early professional era (1934–1955)=== [[File:Flamengo football team 1934.jpg|thumb|Flamengo's team, 1934. [[Brazilian National Archives|National Archives of Brazil]]]] Local advertiser [[José Bastos Padilha]] was elected club president in 1934 and served until 1937. Under his tenure, the club massively improved its popularity in both Rio de Janeiro and the entirety of Brazil. For publicity, he organized a contest for students in schools to create phrases describing Flamengo, from which the phrase ''uma vez Flamengo, Flamengo até morrer'' ("Once you are Flamengo, you are Flamengo 'til you die") was developed and would later be adopted as part of the club's anthem. In 1936 Padilha signed excellent players such as [[Domingos da Guia]] and [[Leônidas (footballer, born 1913)|Leônidas da Silva]] (who would go on to be the leading goalscorer in the [[1938 FIFA World Cup]] as a Flamengo player). These beloved players endeared Flamengo to the public and it is believed that by this time Flamengo was the most popular club in the country. In 1937 Flamengo hired Hungarian coach [[Izidor Kürschner|Izidor "Dori" Kürschner]], who introduced the [[Formation (association football)#WM|WM system]] to Brazil and other innovations from Europe such as training without the use of the ball and playing a more defensive, controlled style. Padilha facilitated the construction of Flamengo's new stadium and current training center, the [[Estádio da Gávea]]. The stadium was inaugurated on 4 September 1938, when [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]] defeated Flamengo 2–0 and Kürschner was promptly fired. In 1938, the five-year split in Rio de Janeiro football over the dispute between professionalism and amateurism was resolved with the merger of the two competing leagues (Flamengo had been a member of the professional LCF – ''Liga Carioca de Football''). In 1939, after twelve years without winning any titles, Flamengo conquered the state championship with a team that would become the basis of the three-time state champions in the 1940s. In 1941, the group played its first international competition, the Hexagonal Tournament of Argentina.{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesf/flamengo-argtrip41.html |title=CR Flamengo (Rio de Janeiro) trip to Argentina 1941 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |access-date=14 March 2019}} In 1942, the first organized supporters group in all of Brazil, Charanga Rubro-Negra, was founded in support of Flamengo.{{Cite web |url=http://www.organizadasbrasil.com/noticia/Charanga-Rubro-Negra-a-primeira-torcida-organizada-do-Brasil-1690.html |title=Charanga Rubro-Negra: a primeira torcida organizada do Brasil |website=Organizadas Brasil |language=PT-br |access-date=14 March 2019}} Flamengo's popularity grew incidentally during [[World War II]] when Brazil's allies, the United States, installed two high-powered antennas in [[Natal, Rio Grande do Norte|Natal]] and [[Belém]] in the north of Brazil to intercept enemy radio signals. They also allowed residents in the North and Northeast regions to receive the radio broadcasts of football matches. As Rio de Janeiro was the national capital at the time and Flamengo was highly successful in the war years with [[Zizinho]] and Domingos da Guia, nationwide support increased. In 1944, Flamengo completed their first ''tricampeonato Carioca'': three consecutive Rio de Janeiro state titles (winning the 1942, 1943, and 1944 competitions).{{Cite web |url=http://www.flamengo.com.br/historia-tri-estadual |title=Os Tricampeonatos Estaduais – Flamengo |website=flamengo.com.br |language=pt-br |access-date=13 March 2019}} The key player of this squad was Zizinho, a player developed at Flamengo and considered the first ever "idol" of the club. Zizinho was transferred to [[Bangu Atlético Clube|Bangu]] just before the start of the [[1950 FIFA World Cup|1950 World Cup]] in Brazil, where he scored twice and the ''Seleção'' finished runners-up. From 1953 to 1955, Flamengo once again won the [[Campeonato Carioca|Rio de Janeiro State League]] three consecutive times. ===Zico and the world champions (1974–1983)=== {{main|1981 CR Flamengo season}} {{football squad on pitch|align=right|GK_nat=BRA|GK=[[Raul Plassmann|Raul]]|RB_nat=BRA|RB=[[José Leandro Ferreira|Leandro]]|RCB_nat=BRA|RCB=[[Mário Caetano Filho|Marinho]]|LCB_nat=BRA|LCB=[[Carlos Mozer|Mozer]]|LB_nat=BRA|LB=[[Léo Júnior|Júnior]]|DM_nat=BRA|DM=[[Andrade (footballer, born 1957)|Andrade]]|RM_nat=BRA|RM=[[Tita (footballer, born 1958)|Tita]]|RCM_nat=BRA|RCM=[[Adílio (footballer, born 1956)|Adílio]]|LCM_nat=BRA|LCM=[[Zico (footballer)|Zico]] ([[Captain (association football)|c]])|LM_nat=BRA|LM=[[Antônio Nunes|Lico]]|CF_nat=BRA|CF=[[João Batista Nunes|Nunes]]|caption=[[1981 Intercontinental Cup]] starting lineup}} Flamengo won their 18th [[Campeonato Carioca|Campeonato Carioca state championship]] in 1978. The following five years would come to represent the club's most glorious era. Brazilian stars like [[Leovegildo Lins da Gama Júnior|Júnior]], [[Paulo César Carpegiani|Carpegiani]], [[Adílio (footballer, born 1956)|Adílio]], [[Cláudio Adão]] and [[Milton Queiroz da Paixão|Tita]] were led by [[Zico (footballer)|Zico]] to become state champions three times in a row – the club's third tri-championship. This run of sustained excellent play pushed Flamengo towards its first [[1980 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian Championship in 1980]]. As national champions, the club qualified to play in the South American continental tournament, the [[1981 Copa Libertadores]], for the first time. The [[1981 Clube de Regatas do Flamengo season|1981 season]] was a benchmark year in Flamengo's history.{{Cite web |url=http://www.worldsoccer.com/blogs/when-flamengo-and-zico-ruled-the-world-341585 |title=When Flamengo and Zico ruled the world |date=14 July 2013 |publisher=WorldSoccer |access-date=1 September 2016}} They advanced through the semi-final group stage of the Copa Libertadores with four victories in four matches.{{Cite web |url=https://www.imortaisdofutebol.com/2012/04/21/esquadrao-imortal-flamengo-1980-1983/ |title=Esquadrão Imortal – Flamengo 1980–1983 – Imortais do Futebol |date=21 April 2012 |language=pt-BR |access-date=13 February 2019}} In the final they encountered Chilean club [[Cobreloa]], also making its Copa Libertadores debut. In the first final at the [[Maracanã Stadium|Maracanã]], Flamengo prevailed (2–1) with two goals from Zico. At the [[Estadio Nacional Julio Martínez Prádanos|National Stadium]] in Santiago the following week, the Brazilian team received a violent reception on the field and fell 1–0 to a [[Direct free kick|free kick]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/deportes/2012/10/27/566724/zico-mario-soto-jugo-con-una-piedra-en-la-mano-en-la-final-de-la-libertadores-1981.html |title=Zico: "Mario Soto jugó con una piedra en la mano" en la final de la Libertadores 1981 |date=27 October 2012 |website=Emol |language=es |access-date=13 February 2019}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.pauta.cl/deportes/las-otras-12-ocasiones-en-las-que-santiago-recibio-una-final-de |title=Las otras 12 ocasiones en las que Santiago recibió una final de Libertadores |date=14 August 2018 |language=es-CL |access-date=13 February 2019}} Equal on goals, a third match was played at the neutral venue of the [[Estadio Centenario]] in Montevideo. Zico scored twice in the first half, sealing the game and the championship. Flamengo were crowned champions of South America on 23 November and qualified for the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], a single match to be played in Tokyo's [[Olympic Stadium, Tokyo|Olympic Stadium]] against [[UEFA Champions League|European Champions' Cup]] winner [[Liverpool F.C.]]. On 13 December 1981, Zico, [[Tita (footballer, born 1958)|Tita]], and [[Nunes (footballer)|Nunes]] took the field for the most important match in the club's history. Two goals by Nunes and one by Adílio (all in the first half) along with a brilliant [[Midfielder|midfield]] performance by Zico earned Flamengo the title of first Brazilian World Champions since [[Pelé]]'s [[Santos Futebol Clube|Santos]], shutting out Liverpool 3–0.{{Cite web |url=http://acervo.oglobo.globo.com/em-destaque/flamengo-da-era-zico-campeao-do-mundo-ao-vencer-liverpool-em-1981-9703290 |title=Flamengo da era Zico é campeão do mundo ao vencer Liverpool em 1981 |date=26 August 2013 |website=[[O Globo]] |access-date=29 November 2016}} The following two years were also marked with success. One more Rio de Janeiro State Championship in 1981 and two back-to-back Brazilian Championships – [[1982 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1982]] and [[1983 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1983]] – closed Flamengo's "Golden Age."{{Cite web |url=https://imortaisdofutebol.com/2012/04/21/esquadrao-imortal-flamengo-1980-1983/ |title=Esquadrão Imortal – Flamengo 1980–1983 |date=21 April 2012 |publisher=Imortais do futebol |access-date=29 November 2016 |archive-date=6 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170206072138/https://imortaisdofutebol.com/2012/04/21/esquadrao-imortal-flamengo-1980-1983/ |url-status=dead }} ===National success and the return of Zico (1984–1994)=== {{main|1987 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A}} [[File:Zico flamengo elgrafico.jpg|right|thumb|[[Zico (footballer)|Zico]] played for Flamengo from 1971 to 1983 and 1985–89, setting several records for the club.]] After spending two years in Italy playing for [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]], Zico returned to Flamengo in 1986 and won his last state championship. Only one month after returning, he suffered a severe knee injury after a violent tackle from [[Bangu Atlético Clube|Bangu]] defender Marcio Nunes, which interrupted his career for several months and affected his form in the [[1986 FIFA World Cup]]. In 1987, Zico was a major contributor to Flamengo's victory in the first edition of the [[Copa União]]. That year, the [[Brazilian Football Confederation|CBF]] was experiencing serious financial and institutional crises and was unable to secure sponsorship to organize the national championship as in years prior. As a result, the thirteen biggest clubs in Brazil (which included Flamengo) reacted and created a new entity named the [[Clube dos 13|Club of 13]] to organize a championship of their own. The CBF originally supported the decision by the Club of 13, but were pressured by other clubs to create a larger national tournament. As a result, CBF placed three additional clubs into the Copa União, regarded the Copa União as the "Green Module", and organized a second "Yellow Module" of 16 other teams. CBF then decided that for the [[1987 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1987 Brazilian Championship]], the winners and runners-up of both modules would face each other in a knockout-style cup to determine the national champion and qualification for the [[Copa Libertadores]], although this decision was made after the beginning of the championship, without Club of 13 agreement. With strong performances from [[Zico (footballer)|Zico]], [[José Carlos da Costa Araújo|Zé Carlos]], [[Renato Portaluppi|Renato Gaúcho]] and [[Bebeto]], Flamengo conquered the Copa União with major victories over [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] and [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]]. However, there was a dispute over whether Flamengo and Internacional of the Green Module would dispute the quadrangular against [[Sport Club do Recife|Sport Recife]] and [[Guarani FC|Guarani]] of the Yellow Module. The Club of 13 clubs had agreed to not participate in the final set up by the CBF, since it was decided while the matches were already being played, but [[Eurico Miranda]], a representative of [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco]], Flamengo's archi-rival and member of the Club of 13, had already signed an agreement with CBF regarding the final, without the board consent. Flamengo still did not participate in the final under the understanding that it would only determine the entrants of the Copa Libertadores and not the Brazilian national champion.{{Cite web |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=0qX8s2k1IRwC&dat=19870904&printsec=frontpage |title=Jornal do Brasil – Google News Archive Search |access-date=14 March 2019}} CBF officially recognized Sport as the sole champion in 1987 and they qualified to the Copa Libertadores. In 2011, CBF retroactively declared Flamengo champion of 1987.{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbf.com.br/futebol-brasileiro/noticias/campeonato-brasileiro-serie-a/cbf-reconhece-titulo-do-fla |title=CBF reconhece título do Fla |website=Confederação Brasileira de Futebol |language=pt-BR |access-date=14 March 2019}} However, Sport later appealed the decision to a Common Justice Tribunal, which is prohibited by FIFA, and CBF ultimately declared Sport as the sole champion of that year, pending appeals from Flamengo, all of which were unsuccessful, and a few years later Sport was officially declared as the champion of the 1987 season.{{Cite web |date=15 June 2011 |title=CBF volta a reconhecer Sport como único campeão brasileiro de 1987 |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/noticia/2011/06/cbf-volta-reconhecer-sport-como-unico-campeao-de-1987.html |access-date=14 March 2019 |website=globoesporte.com}}{{Cite web |date=17 April 2018 |title=Flamengo perde em última instância e Sport é o campeão brasileiro de 1987 |url=https://www.gazetaesportiva.com/futebol/flamengo-perde-em-ultima-instancia-e-sport-e-o-campeao-brasileiro-de-1987/ |access-date=15 October 2022 |website=Gazeta Espórtiva}} Throughout his career at Flamengo, Zico scored 508 goals and was the top scorer in club history before retiring in 1990.{{Cite web |url=http://www.flaestatistica.com/jogadores.html |title=Players records |publisher=Flaestatística |access-date=26 July 2016 |archive-date=12 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171012125045/http://www.flaestatistica.com/jogadores.html |url-status=dead }} Even without its biggest star, the early years of the post-Zico era were successful for Flamengo. They achieved national victory in the second edition of the [[Copa do Brasil]] in [[1990 Copa do Brasil|1990]], defeating [[Goiás Esporte Clube|Goiás]] in the finals. In 1992, Flamengo won their [[1992 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|fifth Campeonato Brasileiro]], defeating [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] across two legs in the final (3–0, 2–2). The team's key player was again [[Leovegildo Lins da Gama Júnior|Júnior]] at 38 years old. ===Mediocre campaigns and relegation escapes (1995–2005)=== After winning the Brazilian League title in 1992, the club entered a major financial crisis and domestic and international achievements became less frequent, although the team still won trophies ranked less in importance. In [[1993 Supercopa Libertadores|1993]], Flamengo lost the [[1993 Supercopa Libertadores finals|Supercopa Libertadores finals]] to Sao Paulo. In 1995, the year of Flamengo's centenary, radio sports broadcaster [[Kléber Leite]] became chairman of the club and signed striker [[Romário]], the current [[FIFA World Player of the Year]], from [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].{{Cite web |date=10 January 1995 |title=Flamengo anuncia contratação de Romário |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/1995/1/10/esporte/20.html |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=Folha de São Paulo}} He joined [[Sávio (footballer, born 1974)|Sávio]] and later [[Edmundo]] to become, as the supporters called, "the attack of dreams".{{Cite web |date=27 August 1995 |title='Ataque dos sonhos' faz a estréia hoje no Flamengo |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/1995/8/27/esporte/15.html |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=Folha de São Paulo}} Even with Romário and other stars, Flamengo's centennial year did not yield major trophies, and the club struggled in the league, finishing 21st of 24. Flamengo only won the [[Taça Guanabara]], the first phase of the [[Campeonato Carioca|state league]],{{Cite web |date=25 June 1995 |title=Campeonato Carioca 1995, Fase Final |url=http://futpedia.globo.com/campeonato/campeonato-carioca/1995/06/25/fluminense-3-x-2-flamengo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210014907/http://futpedia.globo.com/campeonato/campeonato-carioca/1995/06/25/fluminense-3-x-2-flamengo |archive-date=10 February 2018 |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=futpédia}}{{Cite web |date=19 February 2016 |title=Sávio: o ataque dos sonhos do Fla "não podia dar certo" |url=http://esporte.band.uol.com.br/futebol/times/flamengo/100000794725/s%C3%A1vio-o-ataque-dos-sonhos-do-fla-n%C3%A3o-podia-dar-certo,%20savio-o-ataque-dos-sonhos-do-fla-nao-podia-dar-certo.html |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=band.com.br}} and finished runners-up of [[1995 Supercopa Libertadores]]. However, in 1996, Flamengo went undefeated in the Campeonato Carioca. Sávio was the top scorer and best player in Flamengo's victorious [[1996 Copa de Oro]] campaign. The Copa de Oro was Flamengo's first international success since 1981, their third overall international title.{{Cite web |date=16 August 1996 |title=Flamengo Campeão da Copa Ouro de 1996 |url=https://fichadojogo.wordpress.com/1996/08/16/flamengo-campeao-da-copa-ouro-de-1996/ |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=Baú do Futebol}} In 1997 Flamengo finished trophyless for one of the few times in its history, but overall had a good season, finishing fifth in the [[1997 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Serie A]], finishing runner-up to [[Grêmio FBPA|Grêmio]] in the Copa do Brasil on away goals, and finishing runner-up in the [[1997 Torneio Rio-São Paulo|Torneo Rio-Sao Paulo]]. 1998 was another trophyless season, but far worse than 1997; ''Mengão'' finished 11th in the [[1998 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Serie A]], were knocked out of the [[1998 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]] with a 5–0 loss to [[EC Vitoria|Vitoria]], and failed to advance out of the group stages of the [[1998 Copa Mercosur|Copa Mercosur]], although top scorer Romario continued to show individual brilliance with 35 goals from 40 appearances. In 1999, [[Edmundo dos Santos Silva]] was elected club president, and brought with him a massive contract with sports marketing company [[International Sport and Leisure|ISL]].{{Cite web |title=Flamengo e ISL assinam contrato |url=http://www.diariodecuiaba.com.br/arquivo/181299/esportes2.htm |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=Diário de Cuiabá}} Despite a mediocre campaign in that year's [[1999 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Campeonato Brasileiro]], finishing 12th, the club lifted the [[1999 Copa Mercosur]] at [[Estádio Palestra Itália]] after beating Palmeiras 7–6 on aggregate in an exciting two legged final, and were successful at the regional level, winning the Campeonato Carioca over rivals Vasco, who had won the 1998 Copa Libertadores. 2000 was also a mediocre year for the club, being knocked out of the [[2000 Copa Mercosur|Copa Mercosur]] by River Plate in the quarter-finals, and exiting the [[2000 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]] with a heavy 8–2 aggregate loss to Santos. However the club were successful at the regional level again, beating Vasco 5–1 on aggregate for a back-to-back championship. In [[2001 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2001]] league play, Flamengo avoided relegation to the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]] by beating [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] 2–0 on the final matchday.{{Cite web |date=2 December 2001 |title=Em 2001, Flamengo vence o Palmeiras em Juiz de Fora e escapa do rebaixamento |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/bau-do-esporte/videos/v/em-2001-flamengo-vence-o-palmeiras-em-juiz-de-fora-e-escapa-do-rebaixamento/1659155/ |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=globoesporte.com}} Despite near relegation, the club had a decent season overall; they won the [[2001 Copa dos Campeões]] inter-state title, finished runner up in the [[2001 Copa Mercosur]] to [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] on penalties, and beat Vasco again in the state league with a late free-kick goal by [[Dejan Petković]]. With the state title, the club became ''tricampeão'' (three-time champion) for the fourth time in its history (1999-2000-2001) . In 2002, ISL went bankrupt, for reasons unrelated to their contract with Flamengo, and the club was left without its wealthy partner. In the same year, Edmundo Santos Silva was removed from his role as president in a controversial manner amidst accusation of impropriety.{{Cite web |date=7 September 2002 |title=Edmundo: escândalos e títulos no Fla |url=https://esportes.estadao.com.br/noticias/futebol,edmundo-escandalos-e-titulos-no-fla,20020709p68705 |access-date=12 April 2019 |website=Estadão |language=pt-BR}} Lacking the funds to make key signings, Flamengo failed to field competitive teams and narrowly avoided relegation in the 2002, 2004, and 2005 campaigns, with the 2005 season being one of the worst in Flamengo's history; the club only escaped relegation after the arrival of coach [[Joel Santana]], who directed the team to six wins and three draws in nine matches played under his command. Twice in this low period, the team reached back-to-back Copa do Brasil finals, in [[2003 Copa do Brasil|2003]] and [[2004 Copa do Brasil|2004]], ultimately falling to [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] and [[Esporte Clube Santo André|Santo André]] respectively. This Flamengo has also evaded massive taxes in the {{ill|Banestado scandal|pt|Escândalo do Banestado}}.[https://duploexpresso.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/BANESTADO-CC5-VOLUME-III-.pdf BANESTADO-CC5-VOLUME-III][https://duploexpresso.com/?p=113655 BANESTADOleaks: "a lista", finalmente!] ===End of title drought (2006–2018)=== [[File:Adriano Leite Ribeiro.jpg|right|thumb|[[Adriano Leite Ribeiro|Adriano]] celebrating a goal for Flamengo. In 2009 he finished as joint top-scorer in Série A with 19 goals.]] In 2006, Flamengo reached the [[2006 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil final]] for a fifth time, finally managing to conquer the title after losing three previous finals, this time beating rivals [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]]. From 2007 to 2009 Flamengo completed their fifth ''tricampeonato'' in the [[Campeonato Carioca]], and became sole owners of the record for most Carioca titles with 31 ([[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] had 30 at the time). On 9 March 2007, Flamengo received a commemorative date on the [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]] official calendar. Governor [[Sérgio Cabral Filho]] declared 17 November (the day the club was founded) "Flamengo Day". In the 2007 Copa Libertadores, after a near-perfect group stage where the club was undefeated, expectations were high for the team. However, the club was eliminated by Uruguayan minnows [[Defensor Sporting]] in the first knockout round.{{Cite web |title=Flamengo tem currículo de vexames na Libertadores e pode, sim, cair |url=http://espn.com.br/blogs/maurocezarpereira/238483_flamengo-tem-curriculo-de-vexames-na-libertadores-e-pode-sim-cair |access-date=26 December 2023 |website=ESPN |language=pt |archive-date=26 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231226093549/https://www.espn.com.br/blogs/maurocezarpereira/238483_flamengo-tem-curriculo-de-vexames-na-libertadores-e-pode-sim-cair |url-status=dead }} In the [[2007 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Campeonato Brasileiro]], Flamengo spent most of the season in mid table but in the last five matchdays climbed to second place, before being defeated by [[Clube Náutico Capibaribe|Náutico]] 1–0 in the final round and ultimately ending the season third, which was good enough for a spot in the following year's Copa Libertadores. In the [[2008 Copa Libertadores]], Flamengo began their campaign by topping their group. After defeating [[Club América]] 4–2 at [[Estadio Azteca]], in what was Flamengo's first tournament tie against a Mexican club, Flamengo looked to be one of the strongest sides in the competition. However, Flamengo polemically lost the second leg at home 3–0 and were eliminated in the round of 16 again, in what was Joel Santana's final match with the club.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=5 July 2008 |title=Flamengo 0 – 3 América |url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/liga-mx/flamengo-0-3-america_2 |access-date=26 December 2023 |website=Mediotiempo |language=es}}{{Cite web |date=5 August 2008 |title=Fla perde por 3 a 0 e está fora da Libertadores – Flamengo |url=https://www.flamengo.com.br/noticias/futebol/fla-perde-por-3-a-0-e-esta-fora-da-libertadores |access-date=26 December 2023 |website=Flamengo.com.br |language=pt-br}} In the [[2008 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brasileirao]], Flamengo finished fifth, and in [[2009 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2009]] despite being in tenth place in midseason, Flamengo won the league title for the first time since 1992. With this victory Flamengo became five-time league champions, seventeen seasons after their last title.{{Cite web |url=http://www.netfla.com.br/titulos |title=Títulos |publisher=NetFla.com.br |language=pt |access-date=18 August 2015}} The 2009 championship team finished the season with 67 points, the lowest winning point total in Brazil since the current league format was established in 2003. Flamengo were champions despite spending only two rounds at the top of the league: the final two, and the title was won after a dramatic 2–1 comeback victory against [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] in the final round.{{Cite web |date=6 December 2009 |title=Na cabeça de Angelim, Flamengo encontra o alívio e conquista o hexa |url=https://ge.globo.com/Esportes/Futebol/0,,CCF30698-9825,00.html |access-date=12 December 2024 |website=ge.globo.com}} [[File:Ronaldinho Gaúcho.jpg|thumb|left|[[Ronaldinho]] celebrates scoring for Flamengo in February 2011.]]Flamengo experienced a poor run in Série A from 2010 to 2015, finishing better than tenth only once. Following the success of 2009, the club gambled on winning several titles and signed striker [[Vágner Love]] to form a pair with [[Adriano Leite Ribeiro|Adriano]]. The dream of repeating as state champions four times in a row was foiled by Botafogo in 2010. After narrowly qualifying out of the group stage in the [[2010 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]], manager [[Andrade (footballer, born 1957)|Andrade]] was still fired. In their first quarter-final appearance since 1993, after disposing of Corinthians, Flamengo were eliminated by [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] on away goals. Shortly after, Vágner Love and Adriano left the team. A series of coaching changes during the troublesome domestic league saw Flamengo survive relegation, avoiding defeat in their final nine matches, and claim the final berth to the [[2011 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] under manager [[Vanderlei Luxemburgo]]. The blockbuster signing of 2011 was 30-year-old superstar [[Ronaldinho]] from [[A.C. Milan]]. He was joined by Argentine [[Darío Bottinelli]] and Fluminense idol [[Thiago Neves]]. Flamengo won the Campeonato Carioca outright in an undefeated campaign, but captured no other trophies that season: eliminations in the [[2011 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]] by [[Ceará Sporting Club|Ceará]], a heavy 5–0 loss in the [[2011 Copa Sudamericana|Sudamericana]] by Universidad de Chile, and a fourth-place finish in the [[2011 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|league]] left fans feeling that a strong roster had been squandered. The season saw the retirement of Serbian club idol [[Dejan Petković]] as well. In 2012 Ronaldinho sued Flamengo claiming lack of payment for four months and canceled his contract with the club,{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/ronaldinho-leaving-flamengo-over-unpaid-salaries-1.1168247 |title=Ronaldinho leaving Flamengo over unpaid salaries |date=31 May 2012 |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |access-date=12 April 2019}} Thiago Neves returned to Fluminense, and defender [[Alex Sandro da Silva|Alex Silva]] was loaned to [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] after threatening Flamengo with a lawsuit. Vágner Love and [[Ibson]] returned for a 2012 campaign that was worse than 2011: no trophies, a group-stage exit from the [[2012 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]], and an 11th place finish in the Brasileirao. At the end of 2012, Flamengo elected Eduardo Bandeira de Mello as club president for three years. The goal of his term was to improve the club's finances, after an independent audit assessed Flamengo's debt at [[Brazilian real|R$]]750 million.{{Cite web |url=http://espn.com.br/noticia/322462_flamengo-admite-susto-com-a-divida-reconhece-longo-caminho-e-volta-a-recorrer-a-ajuda-de-torcedor |title=Flamengo admite susto com a dívida, reconhece longo caminho e volta a recorrer à ajuda de torcedor |publisher=ESPN |language=pt |access-date=12 April 2019 |archive-date=12 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412175450/http://www.espn.com.br/noticia/322462_flamengo-admite-susto-com-a-divida-reconhece-longo-caminho-e-volta-a-recorrer-a-ajuda-de-torcedor |url-status=dead }} After a typical series of managerial changes, [[Jayme de Almeida]] was appointed as interim manager during which he fought off relegation and won the [[2013 Copa do Brasil|2013 Copa do Brasil final]] against [[Club Athletico Paranaense|Atlético Paranaense]]. It was Flamengo's third Copa title, after 1990 and 2006. Flamengo's [[Copa do Brasil]] title-defense fell short to [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] in the semi-final. However, by 2014, Flamengo was the only club that successfully reduced their debt over the year (down to [[Brazilian real|R$]]600 million) and recorded the highest annual profit.{{Cite web |url=http://espn.com.br/noticia/501393_flamengo-tem-o-maior-lucro-da-historia-do-futebol-brasileiro |title=Flamengo tem o maior lucro da história do futebol brasileiro |publisher=ESPN |language=pt |access-date=12 April 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} In 2015 after an inconsistent start to the Carioca and national league seasons, multiple managers were dismissed and Flamengo failed to qualify for the Libertadores. However, Flamengo had signed [[Paolo Guerrero]] and [[Ederson (footballer, born January 1986)|Ederson]] and were the most valuable club in Brazil with debt now reduced to [[Brazilian real|R$]]495 million.{{Cite web |url=http://espn.com.br/noticia/588131_agora-e-oficial-flamengo-tem-lucro-maior-do-que-o-do-barcelona |title=Agora é oficial: Flamengo tem lucro maior do que o do Barcelona |publisher=ESPN |language=pt |access-date=12 April 2019 |archive-date=12 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412175452/http://www.espn.com.br/noticia/588131_agora-e-oficial-flamengo-tem-lucro-maior-do-que-o-do-barcelona |url-status=dead }} As a result, president Bandeira was re-elected. The club signed fan-favorite [[Diego (footballer, born 1985)|Diego]] in the mid-season and mounted a strong campaign, but could not catch [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in 2016 and finished third in the league table.{{Cite news |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2016/07/fim-de-novela-apos-12-anos-diego-volta-ao-brasil-e-o-novo-reforco-do-fla.htmlpublisher=globoesporte.com |title=Final feliz: após 12 anos, Diego volta ao Brasil e é o novo reforço do Fla |date=19 July 2016 |access-date=19 July 2016 |language=pt |trans-title=Diego Atletico farewell: "Thank you, I'll always be a fan of this club'}}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} 2017 was characterized as the year Flamengo played two major finals at the end of the season but failed to win either. After going undefeated in the [[2017 Campeonato Carioca]], they were eliminated in the [[2017 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] group stage, failing to win a single match away from home but qualifying for the [[2017 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] in third place. In the [[2017 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]], the club reached the final where they lost in a penalty shootout to Cruzeiro. Less than three months later, they reached an unprecedented [[2017 Copa Sudamericana Finals|Copa Sudamericana final]]. They lost away to [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] and drew at home 1–1, losing the title. After the match, a group of Flamengo supporters rioted outside the hotel where Independiente were staying. [[CONMEBOL]] punished the club with two closed-door home matches in the following [[Copa Libertadores]].{{Cite web |url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/apos-confusao-no-hotel-do-independiente-conmebol-vai-abrir-processo-contra-o-fla.ghtml |title=Após confusão no hotel do Independiente, Conmebol abrirá processo contra o Fla |website=Globoesporte |date=13 December 2017 |language=pt-br |access-date=14 March 2019}} In the league, the club finished sixth and qualified for the following year's Libertadores. Nine years after their last Campeonato Brasileiro victory, Flamengo made a title run but fell just short. In [[2018 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2018]] they spent the most rounds as league leader (thirteen) and broke their points record from 2016 (71), but finished runners-up behind Palmeiras. In the Libertadores, after an undefeated group stage, they qualified to the round of 16, where they were eliminated by Cruzeiro. That season, the club recorded their two highest outgoing transfer fees in history: 18-year-old winger [[Vinícius Júnior]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/may/23/real-madrid-vinicius-junior-flamengo-46m-16-year-old-transfer |title=Real Madrid sign 16-year-old Vinícius Júnior from Flamengo for £39.6m |date=June 2017 |work=The Guardian |access-date=4 December 2017}} moved to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in July for €46 million, and 20-year-old [[midfielder]] [[Lucas Paquetá]]{{Cite web |url=https://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2018/10/10/dono-de-70-fla-vende-paqueta-ao-milan-ita-e-ficara-com-r-100-milhoes.htm |title=Dono de 70%, Fla vende Paquetá ao Milan-ITA e ficará com R$ 100 milhões |date=10 October 2018 |publisher=UOL |access-date=11 January 2019}}{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2813944-ac-milan-complete-lucas-paqueta-transfer-player-to-be-introduced-on-tuesday |title=AC Milan Complete Lucas Paqueta Transfer, Player to Be Introduced on Tuesday |date=4 January 2019 |publisher=Bleacher Report |access-date=11 January 2019}} transferred to A.C. Milan for a reported €35 million at the end of the year. President Rodolfo Landim described it as "the worst tragedy the club has ever experienced in its 123 years."{{Cite web |url=https://www.gazetaesportiva.com/times/flamengo/rodolfo-landim-ve-incendio-como-maior-tragedia-na-historia-do-flamengo/ |title=Rodolfo Landim vê incêndio como maior tragédia na história do Flamengo |date=8 February 2019 |website=Gazeta Esportiva |language=pt-BR |access-date=8 February 2019}} The [[Wilson Witzel|governor]] of the state of [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]] declared a three-day period of mourning following the tragedy.{{Cite web |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2019/02/08/football/flamengo-training-ground-fire-youth-team-spt-intl/index.html |title=A fire at the training ground of the Brazilian football club Flamengo leaves 10 dead |last1=Grez |first1=Matias |last2=Klosok |first2=Aleks |date=8 February 2019 |publisher=CNN |access-date=8 February 2019}} Since then, Flamengo fans have sung during the tenth minute of every Flamengo home game in memory of the ten children who died in the tragedy. Most of the changes have been modifications to the design of the monogram, with the latest redesign being unveiled in 2018.{{Cite web |url=https://www.redesignfla.com/ |title=Redesign Flamengo |publisher=redesignfla.com |access-date=2 August 2018 |archive-date=10 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410140148/https://www.redesignfla.com/ |url-status=dead }} The club uses three crests in different situations: the full crest is used as the club's official logo, the rowing crest is used for all rowing related uniforms and equipment, and the white "CRF" monogram is typically the only component of the crest worn on the primary football uniform. It bears a remarkable resemblance to the "RFC" monogram traditionally used by Scottish club [[Rangers F.C.]]. Beginning in 1980, Flamengo wore three white stars aligned vertically along the side of their monogram crest to indicate their three state league tri-championships (1942–43–44, 1953–54–55, and 1978–79–79 Special).{{Cite web |url=https://colunadofla.com/2017/05/evolucao-manto-sagrado-flamengo/ |title=A evolução do Manto Sagrado do Flamengo |date=6 May 2017 |website=Coluna do Fla – Notícias, colunas, contratações, jogos e mais |language=pt-BR |access-date=30 April 2019}} When [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] became Flamengo's kit provider in 2000, their first kit featured the full shield crest with three stars above it for the first time. After the fourth state league tri-championship (1999-2000-2001) and to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the [[1981 Copa Libertadores]] and [[1981 Intercontinental Cup|Intercontinental Cup]] championships, a fourth white star and a gold star were introduced above the crest. (1985–2018)}}]] |} ===Uniforms=== {{Commons|Clube de Regatas do Flamengo kits}} At the 1895 meeting which established the Flamengo rowing club, the club's official colors were decided as blue and gold to symbolized the sky of Rio de Janeiro and the riches of Brazil.{{Cite web |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2015/11/do-azul-e-ouro-para-o-rubro-negro-troca-que-conquistou-o-mundo.html |title=Do azul e ouro para o rubro-negro: a troca que conquistou o mundo |last=Frigols |first=Matheus |website=globoesporte.com |date=15 November 2015 |language=pt-br |access-date=29 April 2019}} The team adopted a uniform of thick blue and gold horizontal stripes. However Flamengo failed to win a single regatta in their first year and gained the nickname of "bronze club." The team colors were perceived as bad luck, and the colored fabric was expensive to import from England. One year after the club's establishment, the official colors were replaced with the current red and black. In 1912, at the request of the Flamengo rowing team (who opposed the use of their uniform by the newly established football team), the football players dressed in shirts divided into red and black quarters which became known as the ''papagaio de vintém'' uniform, named after a particular style of [[kite]]. However the shirt became synonymous with bad luck and was replaced in 1913 by a shirt with red and black horizontal stripes and thinner white bands. This uniform was nicknamed the ''cobra coral'' due to its similarity to the pattern of a [[coral snake]]. This was the uniform worn when Flamengo won their first [[Campeonato Carioca]] title in 1914. The white bands were removed from the shirt in 1916 as the pattern was very similar to the [[List of German flags#German Empire (1871–1918)|flag of Germany at the time]], which Brazil was allied against in [[World War I]]. The rowing team permitted the football team to use their uniform, and Flamengo's traditional football uniform of a red and black striped shirt, white shorts and red-black socks was born.{{Cite web |url=https://mantosdofutebol.com.br/2013/10/historia-camisa-flamengo/ |title=História da camisa do Flamengo |date=28 October 2013 |website=Mantos do Futebol |language=pt-BR |access-date=30 April 2019}} In 1938, Flamengo manager [[Izidor Kürschner|Dori Kürschner]] suggested the creation of a secondary white uniform to "improve the visibility in night matches." The new uniform was approved by the club, and Flamengo became a pioneer of secondary uniforms in Brazil. The white shirt had two red and black stripes across the chest until 1979 when it was changed to a plain white chest with stripes on the sleeves. This was the shirt worn by the team that won the [[1981 Intercontinental Cup]]. Beginning in the 1990s the club began to experiment with their second and third alternative uniforms, sometimes wearing all black or all red shirts.{{Cite web |url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/estreia-com-derrota-do-uniforme-cor-cinza-revive-a-maldicao-das-terceiras-camisas-do-flamengo.ghtml |title=Estreia com derrota do uniforme cor cinza revive a "maldição das terceiras camisas" do Flamengo |website=Globoesporte |date=6 August 2019 |language=pt-br |access-date=6 August 2019}} In 1995 for the club's centenary, a "''papagaio de vintém''" shirt was worn in friendlies. In 2010 uniform supplier [[Olympikus]] introduced a blue and gold alternative uniform which paid homage to Flamengo's original colors and regatta uniform; however it was not well received by fans who likened it to the uniform worn by the fictional satirical team "Tabajara" on the popular comedy program [[Casseta & Planeta|Casseta & Planeta Urgente]].{{Cite web |url=https://colunadofla.com/2017/07/de-volta-as-origens-entenda-por-que-o-fla-lancara-uniforme-azul-e-dourado/ |title=De volta às origens: Entenda por que o Fla lançará uniforme azul e dourado |date=19 July 2017 |website=Coluna do Fla – Notícias, colunas, contratações, jogos e mais |language=pt-BR |access-date=29 April 2019}} In the first half of the [[2009 Clube de Regatas do Flamengo season|2009 season]], the team wore a uniform without sponsorship for the first time in 25 years. Flamengo have continued to traditionally wear red and black striped shirts with white shorts as their primary uniform. On April 1, 2026, Flamengo, through an official statement, announced that it would retire the term "Away" for its traditional white kit.{{cite web|url=https://www.flamengo.com.br/noticias/institucional/nota-oficial-flamengo-aposenta-manto-2|title=NOTA OFICIAL: FLAMENGO APOSENTA MANTO 2|trans-title=OFFICIAL STATEMENT: FLAMENGO RETIRES AWAY KIT|publisher=flamengo.com.br|date=2026-04-01|access-date=2026-04-25}} Although initially believed to be an [[April Fool's Day]] prank, it was confirmed to be true ten days later through a publicity campaign for the new secondary uniform, with the kit being renamed "''Manto 1 Branco''".{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2026/04/10/flamengo-lanca-novo-uniforme-para-a-temporada-2026-veja-fotos.ghtml|title=Flamengo lança novo uniforme para a temporada 2026; veja fotos|publisher=ge.globo.com|date=2026-04-10|access-date=2026-04-25}} {|style="margin:1em auto;" |{{Football kit |pattern_la = _red_hoops |pattern_b = _red_hoops_redvneck |pattern_ra = _red_hoops |pattern_sh = _blanco |pattern_so = _hoops_red |leftarm = 000000 |body = FF0000 |rightarm = 000000 |shorts = FFFFFF |socks = 000000 |title = Traditional primary uniform
